boundary_rationale: This row opens on Babylon's own gods collapsing: “Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Their idols are carried by animals, and on the livestock. The things that you carried around are heavy loads, a burden for the weary.” (web:Isa.46.1) sets the idols of Bel and Nebo onto pack animals as dead weight, their load named with the ordinary carrying-noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) -- a burden common noun in this idol-procession scene, not a verse-initial oracle header of the massa series. The same noun recurs as the idols themselves cannot rescue what they carry: “They stoop and they bow down together. They could not deliver the burden, but they have gone into captivity.” (web:Isa.46.2), spliced at מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte tier) -- the burden noun here matching Isa.46.1's at accent-stripped tier only, not byte (tipcha there against etnachta here) -- closing the tableau on their own captivity. Two root-level devices bridge into the following verses that an English gloss alone would leave undisclosed: the load-bearer participles נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1) answered by הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי רָֽחַם (oshb:Isa.46.3) -- disjoint under consonantal search, the plene and defective spellings each standing in exactly 1 verse at skeleton tier, so the tie is root-level and not a form recurrence -- and the rescue root at Isa.46.2 answered by וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide). Neither device is treated as reason enough to hold this tableau and the following address in one unit, since web:Isa.46.3 turns the discourse from third-person description to a first-person vocative with a named addressee, the stronger seam signal here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading merges this tableau with the divine carry-claim that follows at Isa.46.3-Isa.46.4, since the same carry/bear root spans both, but the fresh vocative address at Isa.46.3 is read as the stronger boundary signal.

I am God, and there is none like me.” (web:Isa.46.9), אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד (oshb:Isa.46.9, byte tier), carry the disputation forward through the appeal opening web:Isa.46.8 and the Cyrus prediction “I call a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country. boundary_rationale: This row opens directly after the closing salvation promise at web:Isa.46.13 on a fresh imperative address to a new addressee: “Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. For you will no longer be called tender and delicate.” (web:Isa.47.1), רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1, byte tier), commanding personified Babylon down from her throne. For you shall no longer be called the mistress of kingdoms.” (web:Isa.47.5) resumes the address to the same addressee named in web:Isa.47.1, continuing the same movement through Babylon's own boast, “You said, ‘I will be a princess forever,’ so that you didn’t lay these things to your heart, nor did you remember the results.” (web:Isa.47.7), the row's own closing verse before the pivot to a fresh summons formula at web:Isa.47.8.
